title: Generalized grievances and differentiated interests
summary: A broadly shared injury can support standing when it is sufficiently concrete and tied to the claimant; a general demand for lawful government ordinarily cannot.
notes:
The assigned materials distinguish an injury shared by many people from an abstract interest in governmental compliance. Sierra Club requires the organization or members to use the affected area. Akins recognizes useful campaign information as a concrete interest even though the same disclosure would benefit many voters. Widely distributed harm therefore does not alone decide standing.

The notes contrast Richardson’s challenge to secrecy of the CIA budget and Schlesinger’s challenge to congressional members holding military-reserve commissions with a contractor denied equal opportunity to compete in Northeastern Florida. They ask whether the doctrinal distinctions reflect the type of legal right, congressional authorization, or the constitutional provision’s structural character. These are editorial questions about coherence; the questions themselves are not additional holdings.

Raines adds a related limit for legislators’ abstract institutional injuries. A student should identify precisely how the claimant is personally affected, what provision protects the asserted interest, and why the requested remedy would matter to that claimant. Simply labeling an injury political, informational, environmental, or widespread will not perform that analysis.
